blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: streets and boundaries

items.t: Maple Ridge land titles register in the New Westminster Land Title District at the New Westminster Land Title Office, so a certificate of pending litigation (CPL) and a court-ordered transfer for a Maple Ridge property are filed against a New Westminster District title.
The nearest Supreme Court registry building named on the Province's courthouse list is the New Westminster Law Courts, Begbie Square, 651 Carnarvon Street, New Westminster.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A foreclosure in British Columbia (BC) must be started by petition under Supreme Court Civil Rule 21-7, and every person whose interest in the mortgaged property is to be extinguished must be made a respondent.

The court may fix a redemption period and, if the amount due is not paid in that period, grant a final order of foreclosure; a party of record may also apply at any time for an order that the property be sold, which is where court-ordered sales come from.
A petitioner who registers a CPL against the Maple Ridge title binds anyone who later registers an interest, and that person need not be served with the petition.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Maple Ridge's 2026 Tax Sale was scheduled for Monday, September 28, 2026, and an owner could pull a property off the list by paying all delinquent taxes by 10 a.m. that day.
Tax-sale purchases in Maple Ridge must be paid in certified funds within two hours of the auction ending — a buyer who wins cannot go away and arrange financing afterwards.

Maple Ridge property taxes are due the first business day in July (July 2 in 2026), and the City puts flat-rate utilities on the same single property tax notice, so arrears on one combined notice are what feed a future tax sale.
Costs in an uncontested foreclosure under Rule 21-7 are assessed under Scale A, the lowest costs scale in the rules' costs appendix.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: development and new projects

items.t: The headline figures the City itself published on April 2, 2026: over 150 rezoning applications and 450 building permits underway, 751 net new homes delivered July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025 (23% above the provincial target of 612), 133 new rental homes built and nearly 300 more approved. Status: City progress report (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: costs and taxes

items.t: The City's own sale costs sit in the tax-sale upset price: outstanding taxes, penalties and interest, plus a 5% administration fee and Land Title Office fees.
Maple Ridge is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so a buyer who leaves a court-bought home empty still owes the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: getting around

items.t: Maple Ridge is served by two West Coast Express commuter-rail stations inside the city, Maple Meadows Station and Port Haney Station, on the Waterfront-to-Mission line.
TransLink's route 791 links Haney Place in Maple Ridge to Braid Station via Maple Meadows Station and Pitt Meadows Station, giving a bus path to the SkyTrain network when the train is not running.

blocks.text: Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: risks and due diligence

items.t: A tax-sale property is a separate risk: the owner keeps a one-year redemption right after the auction, so a tax-sale buyer does not get an unassailable title on sale day.

faq.q: Is a Maple Ridge tax sale the same as a court-ordered sale?
faq.a: No — they are two different sales run by two different bodies. The City's annual Tax Sale auctions properties with three years of unpaid taxes, while a court-ordered sale is a Supreme Court sale inside a foreclosure petition under Rule 21-7. A buyer researching one should not use the other's dates, deposits or redemption rules.

faq.q: How long does a Maple Ridge owner get to redeem after the City's tax sale?
faq.a: One year from the auction date. To redeem, the owner must pay all three years of taxes plus fees, penalties and interest; if the year passes unredeemed, the tax-sale purchaser moves toward title, and property transfer tax is calculated on the property's market value at that transfer.

faq.q: What is the lowest bid the City can accept at its tax sale?
faq.a: The upset price, and nothing below it. The City defines the upset price as all outstanding taxes plus penalties and interest, a 5% administration fee, and Land Title Office fees, and the City itself states it will be an active bidder at the sale.

faq.q: What is a court-ordered sale in Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court Sales?
faq.a: It is a sale of a property supervised by the court after a lender has taken legal action, and the sale needs court approval. Offers are usually made subject to that approval, and other buyers can sometimes bid higher at the hearing.

faq.q: Can I put conditions on an offer for a foreclosure in Maple Ridge Foreclosures and Court Sales?
faq.a: Conditions such as financing or inspection may be limited or not accepted, depending on the lender's and the court's terms. Speak to Jared and your lawyer before you write an offer.
